Last month I spent two weeks in Tokyo for work. There is a lot of food on every street. There aren't many menus in English. On my first night there wasn't much time, so I ate at a small place near the hotel. There were only six seats, and there was no menu at all. The cook just served what he had that day. There are a lot of rules at the table, and I didn't know many of them. For example, there is a special way to hold your chopsticks, and there isn't much talking during the meal. My Japanese colleagues were very patient with me. What surprised me most is that there aren't many trash cans on the streets, but the city is very clean. So my advice is simple. Before a trip, learn a few rules about the food. There is always something new, and people really notice the effort.
